title_as_printed: Tele neuropsychological exploratory assessment of indicators of mild cognitive impairment and autonomy level in Mexican population over 60 years old

Task_Type.reason: An exploratory tele-neuropsychology study that correlates autonomy (IDDD) with screening scores in 47 community-dwelling older adults. There are no diagnostic groups and no classifier. T6 (descriptive clinical study) fits; T4 (correlational) is also supportable.
Task_Type.quote: The correlation between autonomy and cognitive performance variables is analyzed in 47 Mexican subjects over 60 years of age.

Category.reason: The data are neuropsychological screening instruments and informant questionnaires, administered over video call.
Category.quote: The instruments used included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA), Clock Drawing Test (CDT), Test of Word Accentuation (TAP), Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE), and the Activities of Daily Living Questionnaire (IDDD), all adapted into a TeleNP consultation.

Validation_Type.reason: No predictive model; only Pearson correlations.
Validation_Type.quote: The statistical analyses (Pearson's correlation) of the association between autonomy and cognitive variables are presented below

Sample_N_Approx.quote: This research was conducted in a group of 47 persons, 34 of them women (72.3%)

Publication_Year.reason: The issue year is 2023. The paper was accepted 21 November 2022 and carries (c) 2022, so an online year of 2022 would also have matched.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Mexican day-centre attendees; ADNI is not used.
ADNI_Dependent.quote: Inclusion criteria were that they were Mexican citizens, aged 60 years or older
